decisions.reason: After four years, this specialized wafer platform still looks commercially uncertain and likely needs customer-specific effort, so its option value no longer clearly justifies keeping resources tied up.
This is a close extension of the firm's existing wafer business with a clear use case and low carrying cost, so it is cheap to keep available while demand continues to form.
The Cu-interposer offer has technical upside but is a more experimental semiconductor option, and by 2022 a cautious German niche manufacturer would likely cut it without stronger market pull.
An off-the-shelf brand for standard glass and quartz wafers fits the core business and is inexpensive to maintain, so management would keep this option open.
Glass-based circuit boards are farther from the established niche and likely need heavier market development, so weak early evidence makes abandonment the more disciplined choice.
